opus.market_notes: The 3-lane runner genre is one of the most crowded on mobile, dominated by Subway Surfers and Temple Run with huge content and live-ops budgets. A precision/medal twist and neon pixel style aren't enough to stand out without much deeper content, meta progression and polished feel.
opus.summary: This is a solid, well-tested prototype. All tests pass (17-control regression, a runtime smoke test, and a latency bot showing slack drops from 0.45s to 0.10s across 8 stages). The loop is lane + jump/slide + walls, with medals, a daily run, Overdrive and skins. But it is a single ~32KB minified game.js running a fixed loop of 8 short stages (~5 min total campaign), and its HUD is text-heavy with four rows of labels. Owner AI pixel art (runner, drone, barrier, backgrounds, icon) looks decent, but the backdrops have their own baked-in lanes that clash with the canvas-drawn perspective lanes. The store screenshots and the live menu still show flat-rectangle programmer art, audio is fully procedural oscillator beeps/loops, and monetization is an unwired stub.
blockers: Store screenshots in assets/store show programmer-art rectangles and fallback sprites, not the owner art. Real on-device screenshots are needed, and the screenshots claim 6 stages while the game has 8.

Monetization and compliance are stubs. The SkylineAds.showRewarded bridge is not wired, there is no ad SDK, ATT/UMP consent, IAP, analytics or crash reporting, and no privacy policy is hosted at a URL.
Audio is procedural WebAudio oscillator SFX and a synth loop with no real music or sound assets, so it falls far short of genre expectations.

Content is thin for the genre: 8 short authored loops (~5 min campaign) plus Daily and Overdrive, no endless mode or meta economy, and only cosmetic hue-shift skins. Retention will be weak against Subway Surfers-class competitors.

Visual coherence and mobile readability: the canvas-drawn lanes and HUD overlay sit on top of backdrops with baked-in tracks, far gates are tiny near the horizon, and the HUD is cluttered with text. The menu card overflowed horizontally in a 430px-wide headless render. Native iOS/Android projects were never generated or device-tested (cap add not run).
